Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 67, English)
The Four Adhishthatri Devtas (Space, Blood, Vayu, Earth), Hanuman's Dual-T attva Mastery , and Pitru Dosh

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn training/satsang session opening with a systematic teaching on the four devtas that govern the human body (pr ompted by an earlier question fr om "Shivraam Bhaiya"), illustrated extensively thr ough Hanuman ji's own tattva journey , followed by live individual sadhna check-ins, a detailed teaching on pitru dosh, and a closing gr oup prayer/r oll call. This session contains genuine live sangat interaction thr oughout, so it is pr ocessed as a full 3-part document.
1. What Is an Adhishthatri Devta?

An adhishthatri devta/devi is defined as the point/being from which anything originates ("जहां से कुछ भी आरंभ होता है"). In response to an earlier question (from Shivraam Bhaiya), Bhaiya explains that above every human body there are, additionally , four distinct devtas, each governing a dif ferent elemental aspect of the body .
2. The First Devta: Governor of the Space Element

The first of the four devtas is the Adhishthatri Devta pr oper , who controls the practitioner's space (aakash) element . All of a person's past-life (purva janam) powers and subtle bodies (sookshma sharir) flow through this devta. Per this teaching, if a practitioner is able to please/win over this devta, they gain access to a great many accumulated powers — which is why many people specifically focus their worship on the Adhishthatri Devta.
3. The Second Devta: Governor of Blood (Raktha)

The second devta controls blood , not the body in general as commonly assumed — blood itself is described as the true controlling factor behind the whole body . Key points from this teaching: - Blood and its pressure/flow are entirely governed by this devta. - When a practitioner first attains medical drishti , blood is the very first thing that becomes visible; blood's color/quality (bhaav) reveals what is wrong with someone and how far/well blood is reaching dif ferent areas. - At Ashaeiynn, those with medical drishti are described as specifically observing blood flow (rather than bones, which have a dif ferent "scale" of visibility). - Blood is described as capable of both causing and curing cancer , and both causing and resolving heart attacks — nearly all disease is blood-related; continuous healthy blood flow is what keeps the kidneys, liver , and intestines from failing. - Blood constantly regenerates and changes — even skin regenerates roughly every 90 days, and blood roughly every 45 days.
4. The Second Devta's Followers: The Ayurveda / Vata-Pitta-Kapha Tradition

Followers of this second (blood) devta hold that every element of the body should be changed over time, including semen (veerya) — they hold it should not be retained, since physical intimacy is considered necessary; without it, a person is believed to become "dull." Their underlying logic: since the body's elements constantly change and regenerate (like trees shedding old growth before new growth appears), nothing should be artificially held static, including reproductive fluid. This lineage lar gely overlaps with Ayurveda's

vata-pitta-kapha framework , and is referenced extensively in Patanjali's Yoga Sutras ; the mool bandh kriya's very first described element relates to this same principle, though it is often overlooked because it is treated as "normal."
5. The Third Devta: Governor of Vayu (Air/Br eath)

The third devta controls the body's vayu (air) element and its internal pr essure. A person with a strong vayu element is described as extremely powerful ("very muscular ," never lacking ener gy) — this is why vayu putras (sons of the wind — Hanuman ji and Bhima) are so famously strong.
6. Two Types of Br eath: Urdhwagami and Dirghagami

This teaching distinguishes two breath categories: - Urdhwagami (upward-moving) breath, which increases the body's rajasic tattva . - Dirghagami (elongated/extended) breath, which increases both sattvic and tamasic tattva . Controlling dir ghagami breath brings both tamasic and sattvic tattva under control; as urdhwagami breath increases, rajasic tattva rises correspondingly . Each breath type is further said to contain four distinct sub-parts (reserved for a future "mool tatva" session).
7. Oxygen, Brainpower , and the Vayu Devta's Domain

Per this teaching, more powerful breath capacity directly correlates with more available ener gy — it is specifically about oxygen intake , not food intake; food's role is simply to compensate for the ener gy spent breaking down oxygen via hemoglobin. The vayu devta's own domain/"mind" is described (playfully) as located "in the knees" — his influence is very strong from that point downward but does not naturally extend upward, even though logically it should.
8. When Vayu Energy Moves Upward: Genius and Multi-Dimensionality

When a practitioner deliberately redirects vayu ener gy upward (through meditation), that same ener gy enters the brain/head region and the person becomes extr emely intelligent — described as reaching a state of manifold thinking and genius, since a surplus of oxygen reaching the brain activates additional brain regions capable of producing far greater power . A person whose vayu element is this strong and redirected upward becomes multi-dimensional and no longer needs any external space-element powers (i.e., no longer needs the Adhishthatri Devta) — comparable to the "100% brain use" premise of the film Lucy .
9. Hanuman ji's Vayu Tattva Story

Hanuman ji is presented as the definitive illustration of this principle: - He was born with a vayu-pradhan (air -dominant) body , but all of that tattva's force was concentrated below the body rather than above. - Fearing this imbalance, Maiya/the sants bound his lower energy with shakti — leaving him, in his own words, "with nothing, not even a ठेंगा (thumb's worth)." - Maiya told him he still had one path forward: the power of dhyan (meditation) . He first attained gyan (knowledge), then began dhyan, then sadhna — gradually raising his own vayu ener gy from below to above. - The moment that ener gy reached the higher region, he became "master of masters." - When the lower bindings were eventually released, all that lower vayu instantly sur ged upward — because Hanuman ji had already built the internal "channel" for it through prior sadhna, he did not "burst apart" the way Bhima (who lacked that channel) is implied to have been at risk of.
10. Flying Through Astral Power vs. Flying Through the Brain

This teaching distinguishes two methods of "flying" (udan sadhna): the common method invokes an astral being whose hand lifts the practitioner — as soon as that hand lets go, the practitioner falls. Hanuman ji, by contrast, achieved flight and extraordinary ability purely through his own brain/vayu mastery , without depending on any external astral force.
1 1. The Fourth Devta: Governor of the Earth Element

The fourth devta governs the earth (prithvi) element , described as looking almost like carved stone (only the eyes move) and typically visualized seated in a triangular formation. This devta controls the body's magnetic for ce — specifically , one's ability to attract and to repel. All of a person's inherent "pull" (charisma/attractiveness) and repulsion is determined by this devta, not the vayu devta.
12. Vayu and Prithvi Tattva Always Repel Each Other

A key principle: vayu tattva and prithvi tattva always r epel one another — the more vayu element a person has, the less earth element (and therefore attractiveness/charisma) they naturally carry , and vice versa. This is why very physically powerful people ("pehelwan" types) are often described as less personally magnetic — their words carry less natural "rob" (commanding charm), even if they are otherwise very capable.
13. Mata Anjana's Secr et Teaching to Hanuman ji

Per this teaching, Mata Anjana secretly explained this vayu-prithvi repulsion principle to Hanuman ji, helping him realize what he still needed: earth element. Rather than approaching Bhagwan Ram directly , Hanuman ji specifically went to Sita Mata first, asking for her blessing/hand and to accept him as her disciple/ward — completing himself by adding the earth element he lacked. When he then met Bhagwan Ram, both tattvas (vayu and prithvi) combined, completing the full cycle — which is why Ram immediately embraces him ("आओ हनुमान गले लगो").
14. Kul Devta: 1 1 Levels Above the Four Devtas

Above these four devtas — at a minimum of 1 1 levels higher — sit the Kul Devta , described as the ancestral deity standing above one's father's father's father's father (i.e., far up the ancestral line). Every family has one.
15. Choosing and Mastering a Single Tattva

This teaching notes that many practitioners who gain drishti of one of these four devtas fixate on and pursue that specific tattva, achieving great mastery and a distinctive "psychology"/lifestyle built around it — over time, entire cultures and cults have historically formed around devotion to one specific devta/tattva, and each such tradition is described as legitimate and accurate "in its own place." Bhaiya advises practitioners to first identify their own body's natural elemental alignment (vata/pitta/kapha type) rather than relying on generic vitamin panel testing, since that self-knowledge is the real starting point for progress.
16. Live Sadhna Check-In Segment

Following the core teaching, Bhaiya checks in individually with several sangat members on how their personal sadhna is progressing — including reports of visions during Surya Namaskar and a recurring vision of abhishek (ritual pouring) being performed on oneself from above, which Bhaiya confirms is a normal, positive sign, cautioning the practitioner to expect some pressure/intensity but to remain patient, since the overall journey remains a good one.
17. Headache as a Sign of Active Pitru Resistance

When a sangat member reports a severe headache that began that same morning, Bhaiya explains this is a direct sign that her own pitru (ancestral spirits) are reacting against a prayer she recently made against them — since they are seated on her own body/home, they can directly influence her physically . Bhaiya frames this as a genuinely positive sign : the prayer had immediate ef fect, confirming this is the true root cause, and that the pitru's hold will weaken day by day as more havan/ener gy work is done, though some patience and "holding on" through the discomfort is still required.
18. A Sangat Member's Mantra Shakti Sankalp for Named Individuals

A sangat member (referred to as "bahen") confirms with Bhaiya that a specific mantra shakti sankalp (vow/commitment) had been taken on behalf of several named individuals — Nisha Rana, Shruti, Dur ga Shri Majumdar , Suman Mudgil, Monika Arya, Harshbala
Chawla, and Dhara Gule — and Bhaiya confirms this sankalp was indeed made for all of them.
19. Pitru Are Always Paternal — With One Exception

Per this teaching, pitru (ancestral spirits requiring appeasement) are, as a rule, always from the father's side . They come from the mother's side only in one specific circumstance: when the mother's own kul devta has been established in the household, or when the family is actively following the mother's kul devta lineage.
20. Why Removing Pitru Dosh Matters

Removing pitru dosh is described as essential specifically because it clears the way for kul devta's grace to arrive. Once pitru influence is cleared, a person begins to think and act from their own genuine discernment ("think for yourself") rather than being subtly steered, and manifestation begins to happen naturally rather than requiring conscious ef fort.
21. How Pitru Shape a Person's Social Cir cle and Aura

This teaching explains that whether a person feels surrounded by love and connection, or isolated, is substantially governed by their pitru. If a person's aura/personal space contains very few people who stay , or very few people who genuinely care for them, this reflects the pitru's own desire to keep that person close and dependent on them specifically . As pitru influence is cleared, the aura naturally attracts more people who care, because that emotional "vacancy" begins to draw appropriate connections from the astral world — souls connected to the person's own past-life powers/karma are described as naturally , unconditionally drawn toward them once the pitru's grip loosens.
22. A Cautionary Story: A Deceased Guru Possessing a Disciple's Wife

As an extreme illustration of how strongly some ancestral/spirit attachments can manifest, Bhaiya recounts having witnessed a case where a guru, upon leaving his body , went directly to his own disciple's home and entered his disciple's wife (described explicitly as entering "below the navel"). This is of fered as an extreme but real example of how strongly unresolved spirit attachment can manifest, reinforcing why clearing pitru influence matters.
23. Not All Pitru Are Malevolent

Bhaiya clarifies that not all pitru are harmful — some ancestors, when they were alive, greatly enjoyed being surrounded by lar ge gatherings of people (hosting, feeding, and entertaining others), and this same generous, socially warm ener gy can carry over as a positive pitru influence, naturally drawing people toward their descendants. However , Bhaiya cautions that not everyone who lingers around a person does so with good intent — some approach purely for material benefit (" िसफ� पैसे के िलए आ रहा है") and should not be encouraged to stay .
24. The Arun Jaitley Example

Bhaiya references the death of former Finance Minister Arun Jaitley as an example: at the time, Bhaiya observed via dhyan that Jaitley's pitru showed an outpouring of love and support from people around him until the very end of his life — of fered as a real-world illustration of the pitru-vs-purva-janam-shakti dynamic discussed throughout this session.
25. Two For ces Govern How Much Support a Person Draws

Per this teaching, exactly two for ces determine how much social/emotional support and "charisma" (karizma) a person draws in life: either their pitru are working on their behalf, or their purva janam (past life) shakti is. A person cannot manufacture this kind of far - reaching social pull through personal ener gy alone — hence the real, practical need for connection to one's own ancestral and past-life support systems.
26. Closing Gr oup Prayer and Roll Call

The session transitions into a closing group prayer , opening with a roll call of individual sangat members' names (read in a descending alphabetical pattern) for individual blessing/prayer — the visible portion of this session ends mid-roll-call.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Four distinct devtas govern the human body beyond the Adhishthatri Devta discussion itself: (1) Adhishthatri Devta = space element / past-life powers conduit; (2) blood devta = blood flow , disease, and medical drishti; (3) vayu devta = breath, strength, and (when redirected upward) genius/multi-dimensionality; (4) earth devta = magnetic force (attraction/repulsion, charisma). Blood regenerates roughly every 45 days; skin roughly every 90 days — nothing in the body is meant to remain static, per the second devta's tradition (which also holds that veerya/semen should not be retained). Two breath types: urdhwagami (upward, increases rajasic tattva) and dir ghagami (elongated, increases both sattvic and tamasic tattva). Vayu tattva and prithvi (earth) tattva always repel each other — more of one naturally means less of the other; this is why very physically powerful people are often less personally magnetic. Hanuman ji's own journey illustrates raising vayu ener gy upward (via gyan → dhyan → sadhna) to become "master of masters," then separately gaining earth element via Sita Mata's blessing to complete both tattvas. Kul Devta sits at least 1 1 levels above these four devtas, in the far ancestral line. Pitru are always paternal-side by default, except when the mother's kul devta is actively established/followed in the household. Clearing pitru dosh opens the way for kul devta's grace, restores independent thinking, and naturally increases genuine social/emotional connection. Not all pitru are malevolent — some carry over a generous, socially warm ener gy — but not everyone drawn to a person has good intent, and self-interested attachments should not be encouraged. Exactly two forces govern a person's social pull/support in life: pitru, or purva janam shakti — personal ener gy alone cannot manufacture this. Present the second devta's veerya/semen-retention teaching as this specific lineage's own belief system (linked to Ayurveda/vata-pitta-kapha tradition), not as a universal prescription endorsed for all practitioners. Treat the Arun Jaitley reference and the guru-possession story as illustrative real/reported examples of fered by Bhaiya, not as claims requiring independent verification from the bot.
